## 1 Scope {#s-1}

- 1 This document enumerates obligations and procedures of the System Owner & TopLevel Scheme Owner in relation to the NL EUDI Wallet certification system.
- 2 Additionally, the role of Supervisory Body in surveillance of the Trust Framework is described given its strong influence on risks to the EUDI Wallet related services which are subject to certification.
- 3 For The Netherlands, the System Owner & Top-Level Scheme Owner will be the Minister of Economic Affairs.
- 4 Currently, the scope of this document covers supervising the application and maintenance obligations for the the certification (schemes) for Wallet Providers and PID Providers ().

## 3 Governance and System / Scheme Management {#s-3}

### 3.1 Ministry of Digital Affairs governance arrangements {#s-3-1}

- 9 The System and Top-level Scheme Owner role is assigned to Minister of Economic Affairs that will govern these in close collaboration with the Minister of the Interior as with regard to the specificities of the NL National eID Scheme .
- 10 For practical maintenance of the system, the Minister will be supported by a “NL EUDIW Certification System Management Board” that consist of representatives of these respective government actors, as well as government-designated actors on Certification, Accreditation, Supervision, Cyber Resilience and Dutch Law.

### 3.2 Maintenance processes and review procedures {#s-3-2}

- 11 The System and Top-Level Scheme Owner shall ensure the continuous alignment of the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System with the requirements established under Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, the related Commission Implementing Regulations, and optionally the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF).
- 12 The System and Top-Level Scheme Owner shall maintain the scheme by establishing and implementing ongoing monitoring of developments within the European Digital Identity Wallet ecosystem, such as amendments to legislation, technical specifications, and interoperability requirements.
- 13 Whenever changes to the Union regulatory or technical framework or any other material change to the scheme occur, the System and Top-Level Scheme Owner shall assess their relevance and, where necessary, update governance arrangements, the scheme documentation, and operational procedures to maintain full consistency with applicable requirements.
- 14 To keep the NL EUDI Wallet certification System and related schemes aligned, the System and Top-Level Scheme Owner shall integrate information derived from certification, notification, monitoring activities, and statistical reporting to ensure the continued security, trust, and interoperability of the system and scheme.
- 15 Regardless of the reviews which are triggered ad-hoc by significant technical or regulatory updates, the System and Top-Level Scheme Owner shall establish, implement and operate the review procedure conducted on a periodic basis and thereby guarantee sustained compliance throughout the entire operational lifecycle of the scheme.
- 16 For changes to the scheme resulted from security incidents or handling of vulnerabilities – see Chapter 4.

### 3.3 Harmonization of the System and Scheme {#s-3-3}

#### 3.3.1 Opinions and Recommendations {#s-3-3-1}

- 16 According to art. 5c(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, the System Owner shall transmit the draft national certification schemes to the European Digital Identity Cooperation Group whereby the Cooperation Group may issue opinions and recommendations.

#### 3.3.2 Review by Certification System Collaboration Group {#s-3-3-2}

- 18 The EUDIW Certification System Collaboration Group was established to support cooperation among national authorities, national certification scheme owners, supervisory authorities and other competent organizations involved in the certification of the European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDIW).
- 19 In light of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and the implementing acts related to the European Digital Identity Wallet, the Group was set up to contribute to the establishment, maintenance and continuous improvement of a harmonized European framework for high assurance certification of EUDIW solutions.
- 20 The Group targets to be an experienced and competent Collaboration Group with the objective to foster cooperation, information exchange, mutual assistance and development of common practices among its members.
- 21 The Group targets to facilitate the exchange of views, promotes common interpretations of requirements, supports the development of harmonized evaluation methodologies, and seeks alignment of certification approaches across Member States. As an extension of this, the group targets that all this will allow also for a smooth transition towards harmonized EUDIW European Certification Schemes.
- 22 The end-objective of the Group is to ensure a harmonized high level of assurance of the European Digital Identity Wallet throughout Europe, fostering mutual trust, interoperability and consistent confidence in certified wallet solutions.
- 23 As such the System and Top-Level Scheme Owner will discuss the NL EUDIW Certification System and NL EUDIW top-level Certification Scheme periodically with its peers in this Collaboration Group when relevant changes to legislation, threat landscape, technology or other important events or evolutions occur.

## 5 Marks and Labels {#s-5}

### 5.1 EU DI Wallet Trust Mark {#s-5-1}

- 39 NOTE: EUDI Wallet Trust Mark is related to the top-level certificate issued under NL EUDI Wallet certification system according to the procedure specified in NL-TL.
- 40 In accordance with the Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, users shall be provided with a clear means to verify that they are installing or, after activation, actively using a trusted and certified Wallet Solution.
- 41 To achieve compliance with this regulatory requirement, the Wallet Instance of the Provider’s Certified Wallet Solution shall incorporate a dedicated Trust Mark UI view. When a user invokes the Trust Mark within the Wallet Instance, the interface is specified to perform the following operations:
    - Graphics Rendering: It renders the official Trust Mark graphics and/or logo.
    - Informational Text Display: It displays informational text regarding the Wallet Solution certification, which must be localized according to the language settings of the user's device.
    - Certification Connectivity: It provides web links directly to a list of certified Wallet Solutions, as well as to a specific web page containing the certification information of the user's active Wallet Solution.
    - )

### 5.2 Mark of conformity under NL EUDI Wallet Certification Scheme {#s-5-2}

- 44 The NL EUDI Certification System shall establish an official mark of conformity that publicly attests successful evaluation and certification processes for relevant element of the Wallet solution under the NL EUDI Wallet certification system.
- 45 The System Owner shall grant Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) accredited by the Dutch Accreditation Body to perform certification in accordance with the NL-TS, NL-FS, NL-CS and NL-P-P/W-schemes the right to use the mark of conformity.
- 46 Conformity Assessment Bodies – Certification Bodies (CAB-CB) have the right to transfer this Trust Mark to holders of valid certificates issued under these schemes.
- 47 The System Owner shall maintain a register of entities which are entitled to use the mark of conformity, the associated certificates and their status of validity (current, suspended, revoked or expired).

### 5.3 Design and formats {#s-5-3}

- 48 The mark of conformity shall be presented under the following brand: “NL EUDI Wallet certification system”.
- 49 NOTE: Graphical presentation and rules for visual presentation are specified in a dedicated publication by the Minister of Economic Affairs.

- 50 The logo shall be complemented by an appropriate QR code that contains an URL to a portal hosted by the Certification System Owner (which will provide the required information as-well-as additional information about NL EUDI Wallet Certification System and top-level Scheme.

### 5.4 Rules for use the mark of conformity {#s-5-4}

- 52 The mark of conformity may be used only in the following cases:
    - All information related to the NL EUDI Wallet certification system and top-level Certification Scheme issued and distributed by the System / Scheme Owner.
    - Official documents issued by the CAB or the Scheme Owner, such as public reports, lists of certified products or services, statistical data and other public material related to the subject matter.
    - Information platforms (websites, applications, portals dedicated to EUDI Wallet solution related services) linked to the certified product or service Provider, provided that clear indication of relevant certification is presented;
    - Technical and commercial documentation of the European Certified Identity Wallet produced by the holder of certificate, including informational material, product specifications and presentations.
- 53 Any usage of conformity mark which is beyond the catalogue defined in the previous paragraph requires prior approval of the Scheme Owner.
- 54 The use of conformity mark is prohibited in the following cases:
    - Including the mark of conformity in products, services or versions which are not included in the issued certificate.
    - Modifying or combining the mark of conformity with trademarks or other logos,
    - In relation with suspended, revoked or expired certificate which have been issued under NL EUDI Wallet certification system.
- 55 Any improper use of the will be subject to legal action taken.

## 6 Trust Framework {#s-6}

### 6.1 Supervision of Conformity Assessment Bodies {#s-6-1}

- 56 The Supervisory Body designated in accordance with the applicable national legal framework will be responsible for overseeing the activities of Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) that assess and certify products and services according to the NL wallet certification scheme and its subordinate schemes. [That means the following

requirements will be included in national law and replaced by a reference at that time:

- 57 The Supervisory Body shall ensure through both ex-ante and ex-post supervisory activities that CABs continuously comply with the applicable legal requirements, accreditation requirements, certification scheme requirements, and procedures governing the issuance, maintenance, suspension, and withdrawal of certificates.
- 58 The Supervisory Body shall perform its operational tasks including: o Monitoring the ongoing competence, impartiality, independence, and integrity of CABs,

o Reviewing certification processes, assessment methodologies, and certification decisions,

o Conducting both on-site inspections and off-site supervision of CAB activities and records.

- 59 The Supervisory Body shall verify that certificates are issued solely on the basis of sufficient, objective, and documented evidence demonstrating compliance with the applicable certification requirements and that certification decisions are taken in accordance with the rules of the relevant certification scheme.
- 60 The Supervisory Body is empowered to require CABs to provide all documentation, records, assessment reports, technical evidence, and certification decision records necessary to verify the correctness and consistency of certification activities.
- 61 The Supervisory Body shall investigate complaints, appeals, reports of irregularities, and indications of non-conforming certification activities and may perform targeted audits where there are reasonable grounds to question the validity of certification decisions.
- 62 Where deficiencies, procedural failures, or non-compliant certification practices are identified, the Supervisory Body may require the CAB to implement corrective actions within a specified timeframe and demonstrate the effective remediation of the identified shortcomings.
- 63 In cases where a CAB issues certificates without applying the required certification procedures, fails to maintain adequate evidence supporting certification decisions, or otherwise acts contrary to the applicable certification scheme, the Supervisory Body may order the suspension of the affected certification activities and require the review, suspension, or withdrawal of affected certificates where appropriate.
- 64 The Supervisory Body shall cooperate with accreditation bodies, competent authorities, and other supervisory authorities where necessary to ensure consistent oversight of certification activities and the integrity of the certification framework.
- 65 The Supervisory Body shall maintain records of supervisory activities and enforcement measures and shall prepare periodic reports on the performance of its supervisory

activities, including significant findings, corrective measures imposed, and actions taken to safeguard the reliability and credibility of the certification system.]

### 6.1 Supervision of European Digital Identity Wallets {#s-6-1-2}

- 66 The Supervisory Body designated in accordance with Article 46a (1) of Regulation (EU) 2014/910 as modified by Regulation 2024/1183 along with required contact details shall be appointed by national law.
- 67 According to Article 46a (3) of Regulation (EU) 2014/910, the Supervisory Body shall ensure through both ex-ante and ex-post supervisory activities that the providers and their wallets continuously satisfy the regulatory requirements, as well as through taking targeted enforcement actions when informed of any regulatory infringements.
- 68 The Supervisory Body shall perform its operational tasks including:
    - Cross-border cooperation with other supervisory bodies,
    - Requesting from the EUDI Wallet ecosystem stakeholders all necessary for compliance monitoring, o Conducting both on-site inspections and off-site supervision.
- 69 The Supervisory Body is empowered to demand that providers remedy any compliance failures and to suspend or cancel the registration of relying parties within the designated mechanism in cases of fraudulent or illegal wallet usage.
- 70 The Supervisory Body shall coordinate with the data protection authority any action regarding potential rule violations or data breaches.
- 71 In terms of incident response, the Supervisory Body shall report significant security breaches or integrity losses to the competent authorities and single points of contact and inform the public or require providers to do so if such disclosure serves the public interest.
- 72 In line with Article 46a (5) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, if a wallet provider fails to comply with a remediation demand within the timeframe specified by the authority, the Supervisory Body is empowered to order the suspension or complete cessation of the European Digital Identity Wallet provision, factoring in the severity, duration, and consequences of the failure. Such enforcement decisions shall be communicated without undue delay to the European Commission, the supervisory bodies of other Member States, relying parties, and the end-users.
- 73 As stipulated in Article 46a (6) and Article 46a (7) of the Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, the Supervisory Body shall submit an annual report of its main activities from the preceding calendar year to the European Commission by March 31.

### 6.2 Trust Framework: Access & Registration Certificates {#s-6-2}

- 65 To establish a trust framework in the NL EUDI Wallet ecosystem, the

NL EUDIW Certification System Owner shall designate the Access Certificate Provider and the Provider of registration certificates related to Wallet & PID Provider to designated QTSPs.

- 66 These providers wil issue mentioned “certificates” to the PID Provider and Wallet Providers to to ensureauthenticity and validity during interactions of relying parties with Wallet Units.
- 67 These parties will be put on a designated TrustList by the NL EUDIW Certification System Owner. This registration will ensure their trust anchors (comprising public keys and unique identifiers) shall be published in a Trusted List by a designated Trusted List Provider. These lists are hence forward signed and made available through the Commission's List of Trusted Lists, enabling the verification of credentials across the ecosystem.
- 68 The Supervisory Body will be able to suspend or cancel registered Providers upon determining that specific regulatory conditions are not met.

### 6.3 Trust Framework: Registration of Wallet Providers {#s-6-3}

- 75 Following successful completion of relevant certification and additional evaluation processes and verification by the Supervisory Authority, the Wallet Providers will be recognized as a wallet provider in the NL Wallet eID Scheme and notified by NL to the EU to be put on a designated TrustList by the NL EUDIW Certification System Owner.
- 76 The Supervisory Body will also be able to suspend or cancel a registered Wallet Provider upon determining that specific regulatory conditions are not met.
- 77 Note: As a result of suspension or revocation, the status of the affected entity in the relevant Trusted List shall be changed to Invalid. Following this, all valid Wallet Unit Attestations (WUAs) associated with Wallet Units issued by that provider shall be revoked.

## 8 Complaint Handling {#s-8}

- 115 The complaint handling process serves as a structured mechanism for the Top-level, Functional, Cyber Security and Provider Scheme Owners to maintain effective oversight and ensure the accountability of the NL EUDI Wallet Certification Scheme. This procedure facilitates the formal intake, impartial investigation, and resolution of grievances, ensuring that all issues raised by stakeholders are addressed in a systematic manner.
- 116 The procedure commences with a registration of any complaint in the Complaint Management System hosted by the NL EUDIW Certification Scheme Owner and is followed by a formal analysis performed by the respective Scheme Owner upon receipt of a complaint. Should the submission contain formal deficiencies, the Scheme Owner initiates contact the Complainant to request necessary completions or clarifications. Once the application is complete, the Scheme Owner conducts a thorough substantive analysis to determine the scope and validity of the grievance.
- 117 During the investigative phase, the Scheme Owner acts as the central coordinator. Depending on the subject matter, the Scheme Owner may formally request the PID or EUDI Wallet Provider to submit evidence or technical statements related to the case. In instances involving complex technical inquiries, the Scheme Owner may also task the Conformity Assessment Body with providing expert documentation or an opinion regarding the wallet's compliance. Should the initial information prove insufficient to determine potential non-compliance, the Scheme Owner reserves the right to commission dedicated supervisory activities or seek the support of external independent experts at any stage of the process.
- 118 The final stage of the procedure involves the formal resolution and communication of findings. If a complaint is determined to be unfounded, the Scheme Owner issues a notification to the Complainant detailing the rationale for the resolution. If the complaint is found to be valid, the Scheme Owner notifies the Complainant, and, where appropriate, provides relevant information to the PID or EUDI Wallet Provider and the Conformity Assessment Body. Furthermore, in cases of confirmed nonconformity, the Scheme Owner formally notifies the Complainant, the Conformity Assessment Body, the PID or EUDI Wallet Provider, and the National Accreditation Body as well as the Supervisory Authority regarding the initiation of the nonconformity process. This ensures full traceability and adherence to certification oversight requirements, maintaining the integrity and trustworthiness of the national identity framework.
- 119 Where a complaint is lodged in accordance with Article 25 of the Act on the National Cybersecurity Certification System, the Scheme Owner shall cooperate with the National Cybersecurity Certification Authority and provide it with the information necessary to assess the complaint.

## 9 Secured Exchange of Information {#s-9}

- 121 The Scheme/System Owner, the EUDICG, the European Commission, CABs and all other stakeholders shall ensure the security and protection of trade secrets and other confidential information, including business secrets, as well as the preservation of intellectual property rights, All interested parties shall implement appropriate and compliant technical and organizational measures for protecting information.
- 124 The System Owner shall designate and adopt the cryptographic mechanisms specified in the relevant technical specifications referred to in the applicable regulations, in strict compliance with the security requirements stipulated in Annex I of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979.
- 125 These mechanisms are mandated to ensure the security, integrity, and confidentiality of data exchanged within the EUDI Wallet ecosystem and shall be adhering to the common Union-wide cryptographic standards required for cross-border interoperability.
- 126 The System Owner shall maintain and disseminate an inventory of applicable cryptographic mechanisms and technical applications designated for use by Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) and Applicants.
